title: Berlin woolwork rose panel
subtitle: A framed panel worked from a Victorian charted rose in tent stitch on 13-count canvas
excerpt: This small framed panel reproduces a Victorian Berlin woolwork rose design. The rose is worked in six shades of red and pink, with a full surround of dark leaves, all in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas. Finished size is 15 by 18 cm.
sourceNotes: Rose pattern from Weldon's Practical Needlework, Berlin work series (1887). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Berlin work chapter. Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746.

glossaryTerms.definition: The gradual transition from one shade of wool to the next across adjacent stitches, used in Victorian Berlin woolwork to model the curves of petals and leaves.

heroPrompt: A framed needlepoint panel showing a rich red Berlin woolwork rose with dark green leaves on a black background, mounted and framed in mahogany-coloured wood, natural museum light.

content.text: This panel reproduces a charted Victorian rose in the Berlin woolwork tradition. The design is 78 by 94 holes on 13-count canvas, finishing at 15 by 18 cm. Six shades of red and pink build the rose through
wool shading
. Four shades of green give depth to the surrounding leaves. The background is worked in black.

content.text: Palette
Rose 1: DMC 814 / Anchor 45: dark garnet
Rose 2: DMC 815 / Anchor 43: medium garnet
Rose 3: DMC 816 / Anchor 1005: garnet
Rose 4: DMC 817 / Anchor 13: very dark coral red
Rose 5: DMC 3350 / Anchor 59: ultra dark dusty rose
Rose 6: DMC 3716 / Anchor 25: very light dusty rose
Leaf dark: DMC 890 / Anchor 218: ultra dark pistachio green
Leaf medium: DMC 987 / Anchor 244: dark forest green
Leaf light: DMC 988 / Anchor 243: medium forest green
Leaf highlight: DMC 472 / Anchor 253: ultra light avocado green
Background: DMC 310 / Anchor 403: black
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a scroll frame. A panel of this size worked entirely in basketweave distorts less than a continental piece, but a scroll frame prevents the large black background area from puckering.
Stitches used
Basketweave tent stitch
throughout. Work the motif first, background last.
Working method
Mark the design boundary on the canvas and draw a 10-hole grid in pencil to help place the charted motif.
Work the rose from the centre outward. Use the darkest shade at the inner petals. Lighten through the six shades to the palest shade at the outer petal tips.
Work the leaves, placing the darkest shade at the outer edges and the lightest highlight on the central vein of each leaf.
Fill the black background in basketweave. This is the largest area; working it in basketweave avoids ridging.
Block the finished canvas by dampening and pinning square overnight.
Finishing
Lace the blocked canvas over the acid-free mounting board and fit into a picture frame. A wide, dark wood or gilt frame suits the Victorian character of the design.
What to try next
A Berlin woolwork parrot or butterfly uses the same six-shade palette technique. Both motifs appear frequently in Victorian charted sources and offer more complex shading across curved forms.
